solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bachelor in repeated shows ridiculously wins everything

indicators.note: the letters are treated absurdly, i.e. thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bachelor appearing again and again in reruns somehow scoops every prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' looks like it is telling you to double 'shows', but both words are simply raw letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep the board is an idiom for taking every prize or victory on offer.

clue.text: Ambitious types that may be found in mobile class, mostly rich?

indicators.note: founding is casting metal into a new shape, so the letters are recast in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: only most of the word rich is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its end

explanation.surface: Status-seekers are what you'd expect among a socially mobile, nearly wealthy class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' reads as the anagram signal but is itself fodder; the rearranging is signalled by 'found', in the foundry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Social climbers are people ambitious to rise in social standing, a fair gloss of ambitious types.

clue.text: Provide big picture in general, though disorganised

indicators.note: a disorganised word has its letters out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vague instruction to give an overview in general terms, however muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big picture' suggests an overview, but here it is literal: to make a picture bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarging a photograph means producing a bigger print of it.

clue.text: Boy in family flanked by men on board in uncle's business

indicators.note: something flanked by others has them on either side, so one piece sits between the two others

parts.note: two chessmen: the lowliest piece and the most important one, set side by side
a brother is a boy in the family, shortened to bro

explanation.surface: A family scene with a son surrounded by chessmen, set in an uncle's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against goods left with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawnbroking is the trade of lending against pledged items, and uncle is a slang name for such a lender.

clue.text: Monarch's supporter taken by surprise in hearing

indicators.note: what is heard rather than seen, so a word is swapped for one that sounds the same

parts.note: thrown means disconcerted or caught off guard

explanation.surface: A royal's backer is caught off guard during a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' hints at a loyal follower, but it is the seat that literally supports the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The throne is the ceremonial chair on which a monarch sits, literally holding the king or queen up.

clue.text: One who acts badly as Duke in role I've revised

indicators.note: a revised text is reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An actor playing a duke in a rewritten part performs poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts badly' suggests a weak actor, which the theatrical surface reinforces; the answer is a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a person who commits wicked deeds, so their actions are bad.

clue.text: Lout starts off on all fours

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their initial letters, read off one by one

parts.note: the three words whose initial letters are taken

explanation.surface: A yob begins crawling about on hands and knees.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, boorish man, close in meaning to a yob.

clue.text: More inclined to stop working without raise? Just the opposite

indicators.note: here in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps another
tells you to swap the roles, so the raise goes outside and stop working goes inside

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as children or animals
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone is keener to retire if there's no pay rise on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue would put the raise inside; 'Just the opposite' reverses that, so the word for raise surrounds the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier means more willing or more prepared to do something, which matches being more inclined.

clue.text: Discussion among people whose positions may be very far apart

definitions.meaning: a meeting or conference between several participants

definitions.text: whose positions may be very far apart
definitions.meaning: sounds like strongly opposed views, but means participants physically distant, linked by phone or video

explanation.surface: A debate between parties whose opinions are poles apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positions' tempts you to think of opinions; it really means locations.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting held by phone or video link lets participants in distant places confer together.

clue.text: Common complaint, sore back, creating period of tension

parts.note: the common cold is the most ordinary ailment

indicators.note: read backwards, so the word for sore is turned round

parts.note: raw skin is sore

explanation.surface: A sniffle and an aching back combine to make a stressful spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore back' looks like a medical complaint, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long standoff between the USSR and the West, a lengthy stretch of hostility without fighting.

clue.text: Blow up new tyre needing air that is lying around

indicators.note: one piece lies round the outside of the others

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
a flat is a deflated tyre

explanation.surface: Pump up a new tyre that's gone soft, says a motoring instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' could mean explode, but here it means fill with air, which fits the tyre picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate something is to fill it with air or gas, which is what blowing up a balloon means.

clue.text: Lawyer oddly lacking in Scottish town

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are missing, leaving only the even ones

parts.note: taken as written; only its even-numbered letters survive

explanation.surface: A Scottish town where, strangely, there are no lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a town on Scotland's west coast, known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland, the county town of Ayrshire.

clue.text: Person called to order drink

definitions.meaning: a monk of the Order of St Benedict, i.e. someone with a vocation to that religious order
a herbal liqueur originally made by ... monks

explanation.walkthrough: 'called to order' sounds like a chairman silencing a meeting; here it is a religious calling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a monk of St Benedict's order and the brandy-based liqueur named after them.

clue.text: European producing strangely innocent short story

indicators.note: strange arrangement: the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A European writes an oddly naive little tale.
explanation.walkthrough: To Britons, 'Continental' means from mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental describes someone or something from mainland Europe as opposed to Britain.

clue.text: Religious education included in Conservative party's statements of belief

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a do is a party; the possessive gives the plural-looking form

explanation.surface: Tory manifestos include a line on RE in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the school subject; C abbreviates Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or principles, from the Latin opening word of the Creed.

clue.text: Artist, architect, and engineer putting sign outside on a road

indicators.note: the sign wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A polymath puts up a road sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was a Renaissance polymath famed as painter, designer and inventor.

clue.text: Climber writes a novel about island

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the island's letter
novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer pens a book about an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a woody vine that climbs walls and pergolas, a classic climbing plant.

clue.text: Mischief-maker not breaking law, it's understood

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite or child
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who stays within the law, it's understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's understood' reads like a chatty aside but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied without being stated outright, so it is tacitly grasped.

clue.text: For a sailor getting a raise, equitably distributed?

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters reads them upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Backing a seaman's request for a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO RATA is Latin for in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata means proportionally, so each share is in proportion to what is due.

clue.text: Row across river to provide warning

indicators.note: one piece goes across another, i.e. lies inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
the Po is the long river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Rowing over a river to raise the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like rowing a boat, especially beside 'river', but it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a confidential warning or piece of advance information.

clue.text: Unfashionable hairstyle making sudden appearance

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a crop is a short haircut

explanation.surface: A dated haircut suddenly turns up again.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is an emergence, a rock formation or occurrence that pops out above the surface.

clue.text: Screen part in which mysterious smile attracts most viewers

definitions.meaning: one of the angled slats in a shutter or screen

definitions.text: in which mysterious smile attracts most viewers
definitions.meaning: the Paris museum where the Mona Lisa's enigmatic smile draws the crowds

explanation.walkthrough: The mysterious smile is the Mona Lisa's, the most visited painting in the Louvre museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a slat in a ventilating screen and the great Paris art gallery.

clue.text: Convincingly made clear what bacon is for dependants

definitions.meaning: to bring a point home is to make it felt clearly
a breadwinner brings home the bacon, i.e. earns money for the family

explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the idiom 'bring home the bacon', earning the household's living.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both driven home as a point and carried back to the house, as wages for a family.

clue.text: Highly rocky situation politician isn't ending

indicators.note: the word loses its ending, its final letter

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A precarious spot for a politician whose career isn't finished.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a craggy outcrop on a hill summit, so a rocky place high up.

clue.text: University official is shown round a nuclear facility

indicators.note: the official goes round the other letter, as a visitor is shown round a site

parts.note: a rector heads some universities and colleges
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university head is given a tour of a nuclear plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the plant where nuclear fission is controlled to produce energy.

clue.text: For example, a little rum baba

explanation.walkthrough: 'rum baba' is a cake, but the two words belong to different definitions; baba is baby talk for a little child.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is both a small dram of liquor and a toddler.

clue.text: Check age and name for old-timer

parts.note: to vet is to check or screen
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Verify someone's age and name before registering an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience, a seasoned old hand.

clue.text: Incomplete screening — biased excerpt from the clip seen

parts.note: partial means favouring one side

indicators.note: an excerpt is a stretch cut out of a longer text, so only the letters inside these words are kept

parts.note: the letters of these words, with the outer ones trimmed away, leave the second word of the answer

explanation.surface: A one-sided film review based on a short clip.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word sits inside 'thE CLIP SEen'. 'screening' suggests showing a film; here it is the moon screening the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In a partial eclipse only part of the sun is blocked out, so the covering is not total.
